page.layout: One column of running text, with the page number and running head at the top. The right edge of the scan is cropped, so some line ends are cut off. Below the text the section VII paragraph ends with the Syriac line and "Epho tunica Sa-". No margin notes and no catchword.

main_text.p: vertendumqve, perfectus est, cuju[?] imperativus est [illegible, ~5 letters] perficere. I[?] Maronitarum autem Rituali verbum hoc abest, adeoqve possunt illa redd[?] qvoqve imperativè, & constare hoc vi[?]detur ex ordinatione Episcopi, ubi e[?] verba sunt praesentis temporis modi i[?] indicativi, legiturqve [illegible, ~6 letters] or[?]dinatur, &c. Sed hoc in tuo exemplari Ritualis Maronitarum diligenter animadverte, scilicet illud esse imperfectum & quasi compendium & indicem nam plures preces indicantur tantùm tamqvam ex alio codice recitandae. Confer illud cum exemplari Illustrissimi D[?] Cancellarii Petri Seguierii, & hoc verissimum esse comperies.

VII. [illegible, ~4 letters] apud Nestorianos & Orientaliores Syros accipitur pro A-mictu, qvi est pars indumenti Sacerdotalis, qvo tegitur caput; at apud no-stros usurpatur pro pallio Sacerdotali[?] [illegible, ~4 letters] Amictus. [illegible, ~3 letters] Epho tuni-ca Sa-

page.notes: The Syriac words (in the first paragraph, in section VII and in the two italic glosses "Amictus" and "Epho") are not legible letter by letter at this scan resolution, so they are marked illegible. The right edge of the scan is cropped: words cut off there are given only as far as they are visible and marked [?]. Hyphens at line ends are not visible in the cropped area, so split words are joined whole (imperfectum, exemplari, Confer, verissimum, ordinatur). The asterisk after "comperies." is a printer's ornament and is left out.
